meta.environment: macOS 26.4 (arm64), CPython 3.12.14. Every budgeted metric here is a call count rather than a duration, so it does not depend on this machine: the same numbers were measured on CPython 3.11.16, the other interpreter the CI test matrix runs.

not_applicable.p95_ms: No hosted route. nearmiss is a CLI/library that publishes a static artifact; the only server it ships is the local read-only `nearmiss serve` used for the synthetic methods UI, which is not deployed. PERFORMANCE-STANDARD.md is explicit that a library with a hot path records a benchmark regression check instead, and that is what the work-unit metrics below are.
not_applicable.llm_first_token_ms: No LLM or model component anywhere in the codebase. The AI Evaluation standard is declared N/A for the same reason in docs/adr/0004-standards-applicability.md and in the README's Standards Conformance table.
not_applicable.llm_full_response_ms: No LLM or model component anywhere in the codebase; see llm_first_token_ms.
not_applicable.lighthouse_performance: Not budgeted here on purpose, and not silently dropped: the shipped HTML is gated by `make accessibility` and `make web-check` (structural WCAG plus axe-core in jsdom), and a browser-rendered Lighthouse run is one of the named open items in the README's Accessibility row. Wiring a Lighthouse score into this file before that run exists would put a number here that nothing measures.
not_applicable.js_kb_gzip: Same run as lighthouse_performance: the resource budget is a Lighthouse-CI assertion, and no Lighthouse-CI run exists yet. The published pages ship hand-written JS with no bundler and no framework, so there is no build step whose output could drift unobserved in the meantime.
not_applicable.wall_clock_total_s: Measured on every run and printed by `make bench`, published in docs/PERFORMANCE.md, and deliberately not merge-blocking: GitHub's shared runners vary by far more than the 10% band, so a seconds budget would be either muted or red for reasons unrelated to the diff. The work-unit metrics below are the exactly reproducible half of the same benchmark. What that leaves uncovered -- a constant-factor slowdown inside an unchanged number of calls -- is stated in perf/README.md rather than implied away.
